title: Relational databases
brief: Accepted introduction, preserved. Establish tables and relationships, query grain, constraints, atomic purchase, concurrent stock and relational fit; offer several next questions.
outcomes: Explain how shared relational facts support queries and guarded changes.
Choose a first route from design, queries, concurrency, performance, application work or recovery.
entry: An engineer familiar with an application request and stored data; no database vocabulary assumed.

heading.title: Tables and keys
heading.brief: Accepted explanation of tables, row identities and references. Child placements are planning annotations, not requests to alter the introduction.

heading.title: Relations and values
heading.brief: Continue from an identity to deliberate row design.

nested_article.title: Relations, keys and normalisation
nested_article.brief: Choose one fact per row and identities that preserve meaning when the shop changes.
outcomes: Design keys and references from row meaning
Explain dependencies, anomalies and justified duplication
nested_article.entry: Introduction: tables, IDs, order lines and agreed prices.

heading.title: What an order contains
heading.brief: Accepted separation of orders and numbered lines, with the agreed price preserved on each line.

heading.title: Asking a question
heading.brief: Accepted SELECT, filtering, ordering, receipt join and per-order totals.

heading.title: Joining lines to products
heading.brief: Continue from one result row per order line to joins with independent many sides.

nested_article.title: Joins and the meaning of a result row
nested_article.brief: Construct a result whose rows mean exactly what the question requires.
outcomes: Predict row multiplication and missing matches
Build a correct still-due report and absence test
nested_article.entry: Introductory JOIN, GROUP BY and NULL; keys and value semantics.

heading.title: From lines to totals
heading.brief: Continue from a grouped total to grouped and per-row calculations.

nested_article.title: Aggregates, windows and ordered results
nested_article.brief: Choose grouped and per-row calculations with explicit ordering and peer semantics.
outcomes: Derive totals without changing the intended grain
Select deterministic windows, rankings and frames

heading.title: Application queries
heading.brief: Route annotation from explained SQL into a real application request.

nested_article.title: SQL at the application boundary
nested_article.brief: Keep query meaning and transaction ownership intact across the application connection.
outcomes: Separate values from SQL structure
Handle one request’s connection, result, error and cancellation coherently

heading.title: Rules at the table
heading.brief: Accepted primary, foreign, unique, null and row checks, with their domain limits.

nested_article.title: Constraints and tenant boundaries
nested_article.brief: Turn invariants into enforceable schema boundaries and identify the rules that require a protocol.
outcomes: Express row, identity and reference rules
Separate tenant integrity, access control and concurrent invariants
nested_article.entry: Keys, NULL and transactions from the introduction.

heading.title: A purchase as one change
heading.brief: Accepted stock/order/line atomicity, pending payment, durability and external-effect boundaries.

heading.title: Durable commit
heading.brief: Continue from the crash promise into log ordering and recovery.

nested_article.title: Write-ahead logs and crash recovery
nested_article.brief: Explain the ordering that makes a committed change recoverable after a crash.
outcomes: Distinguish durable log from flushed data pages
Separate restart recovery from recovery after storage loss
nested_article.entry: Atomic transactions, row versions and storage pages.

heading.title: An uncertain reply
heading.brief: Continue from lost commit acknowledgement into one identifiable purchase.

nested_article.title: Retries when a commit reply is missing
nested_article.brief: Recover a purchase safely when the client cannot tell whether it committed.
outcomes: Distinguish known aborts from an unknown commit outcome
Reuse one request identity and reject conflicting payloads
nested_article.entry: Transactions, unique keys and application connection ownership.

heading.title: Two buyers, one mug
heading.brief: Accepted saved-write race and guarded PostgreSQL Read Committed schedule; no broader isolation assertion.

nested_article.title: Transactions and isolation
nested_article.brief: Choose transactions and isolation from the invariant the writers must preserve.
outcomes: Distinguish atomicity, snapshots and serial outcomes
Choose a sound protocol for one-row and multi-row limits

heading.title: Where relational databases fit
heading.brief: Accepted fit, costs and server/distributed deployment distinctions. These child carriers organise the commissioned collection; they do not add headings to the accepted source.

heading.title: Affordable queries
heading.brief: Continue from correct answers into the cost of producing them.

nested_article.title: Indexes and access paths
nested_article.brief: Understand which work an index saves and what every maintained entry costs.
outcomes: Derive useful key order and selectivity from a query
Weigh read savings against writes, space and upkeep
nested_article.entry: Keys, result semantics and ordered queries.

heading.title: Copies and freshness
heading.brief: Continue from durable state into another copy and its read contract.

nested_article.title: Replicas, lag and read routing
nested_article.brief: Route reads from the freshness and failure promises each copy can meet.
outcomes: Distinguish received, durable and replayed progress
Design read-your-write routing and account for lag and retention
nested_article.entry: Commit durability and application request identity.

heading.title: A changing schema
heading.brief: Continue from explicit shared meanings into compatible live changes.

nested_article.title: Live schema changes and backfills
nested_article.brief: Change a schema through compatible states while callers and existing rows keep changing.
outcomes: Design expand, migrate and contract around real callers
Prove a backfill converged despite races and late rows
nested_article.entry: Constraints, application transactions and bulk changes.

heading.title: Distribution boundaries
heading.brief: Continue from one service into partition ownership and local work.

nested_article.title: Sharding and distributed SQL
nested_article.brief: Choose a distribution boundary from local work, invariant scope and the actual bottleneck.
outcomes: Compare table partitioning, replicas and sharding
Derive locality, skew, fan-out and distributed coordination from the key

heading.title: Distributed commit
heading.brief: Develop atomic outcomes across partition owners.

nested_article.title: Transactions across partitions
nested_article.brief: Explain atomic outcomes across partitions without confusing them with replicated agreement.
outcomes: Distinguish replica consensus from transaction commit
Recover a distributed decision after coordinator loss
nested_article.entry: Transactions, crash records, sharding and write authority.

heading.title: Distributed snapshots
heading.brief: Develop common observations and safe historical reads.

nested_article.title: Time, snapshots and distributed reads
nested_article.brief: Read related partitions at a safe common history while preserving the distinction between observation and authority.
outcomes: Explain a common distributed snapshot
Compare clock uncertainty, logical timestamps and safe historical reads
nested_article.entry: Isolation, replicated progress and distributed commit.

heading.title: Regional placement
heading.brief: Develop geography, authority and survival budgets.

nested_article.title: Regional placement and survival
nested_article.brief: Place data and voting replicas against a stated latency and survival budget.
outcomes: Derive quorum survival from failure domains
Trace remote coordination introduced by local data and global invariants
nested_article.entry: Replicas, authority, sharding and distributed commit.

heading.title: Cluster change
heading.brief: Develop live movement and compatibility boundaries.

nested_article.title: Rebalancing and cluster change
nested_article.brief: Move replicas, data and software while continuing to preserve one authoritative history.
outcomes: Explain catch-up and safe membership change
Budget movement and decommissioning without using lost redundancy as capacity
nested_article.entry: Sharding, replicated authority and regional failure budgets.

heading.title: Sources and further reading
heading.brief: Preserve the accepted source and illustrative-model statement; implementation writing will record its own versions and execution evidence.
